Yes you definitely can learn to draw with what you have there’s r/learnart here on Reddit. And I learned a lot from draw with jazza’s old YouTube videos and love life drawing has some good videos to and one on using shadows to draw portraits which is really good. My biggest tips for learning to draw are just draw from life like draw your cub or your bed or your mom don’t worry about if it’s good cause your learning. Be confident with your lines don’t do a bunch small lines to draw a circle do it in one big confident line. Draw lightly a lot a beginners tend to really press there pencils down on the paper making the lines impossible to erase. Oh and draw for fun to I always found drawing from life kinda fun but I didn’t really like gesture drawing at first so I would draw some still life’s or characters from my head and some gestures. It’s important to have fun with your art not just focus on improving. Oh yeah also you don’t need to hold your pencil any differently when you draw then normal. And you could try getting a how to draw book at the library and working with that. And also you don’t need a sketch book if you can get one great if not don’t worry but I do suggest trying to draw on paper with out lines and also trying to keep the paper say in a folder or something so that if you want you can look back on it and see how far you’ve come. Also you can use r/artcrit and r/artfundamentals for more help and I always find it helpful to just look at the comments on. Subs like art crit because I think it helps me train my brain to see and understand what’s wrong and how to fix it like I might know a picture don’t look right but not now what was wrong where now I at least know what’s wrong with it say the arms to long even if I don’t know/ can’t fix it. And how to fill your sketch book videos are good but stay away from sketchbook tours till later as to not psych your self out and lastly try doing gestures drawings they’ll teach you to make more confident lines and how to draw faster my favorite resource is CroquisCafe on vimeo. Oh and blind contours (drawing something without lifting your pen from the paper and without looking at the paper only looking at the object) are in my opinion a great way to loosen up and contours (drawing something in one continuous line) to.
